meta.title: Make a Mark Brussels
meta.description: A one-day make-a-thon where creative makers and Brussels social organisations work together on communication, design, and digital challenges. Join the 2027 edition.

makers.heading: Info for Makers

steps.title: Friday evening
steps.text: We all come together to plan and get to know each other. To make sure everyone can go in turbo creative mode Saturday.

steps.title: All day Saturday
steps.text: You'll spend the whole of Saturday collaborating in a team, tackling a creative challenge for the central case. We'll provide WiFi, food, drinks, and great company to keep you energized throughout the day.

steps.title: Selected in advance
steps.text: We select Makers in advance, ensuring we form the most effective teams to tackle the challenges. We'll let you know at the end of January if you got selected. A few weeks after that you'll meet your team members and the organisation to discuss their challenge, in a one-hour meeting on an evening in the first week of March.

makers.closing: Please make sure you can make it.

about.heading: The people behind Make a Mark
about.intro: Make a Mark Brussels is part of the global Make a Mark movement. The local team brings volunteer makers and social organisations together for a day of shared creative work.

organisers.name: Gwen Dubois
organisers.role: The instigator. An interior architect and creative activist from Jette.

organisers.name: Piet Lambrecht
organisers.role: Organising it from the start with Gwen. Until recently he led the communication of Muntpunt.

organisers.name: Frederik Vincx
organisers.role: A Maker at many editions before he joined the organisers. He builds digital products for social organisations in Brussels.

organisers.name: Bernard Polet
organisers.role: A Maker at many editions before he joined the organisers. He founded //gaggarin//, a gallery in the Brussels Canal Zone.

edition.title: Make a Mark for Brussels youth
edition.photoAlt: Makers and organisers of Make a Mark Brussels in a courtyard, photographed from above
edition.body:
Make a Mark brings volunteer makers together with Brussels social organisations for one day of creative work on a real communication, design, or digital challenge.

The 2027 edition centres on organisations working with young people in Brussels. The event date is confirmed; venues and application details are still being prepared.
edition.html:
Make a Mark brings volunteer makers together with Brussels social organisations for one day of creative work on a real communication, design, or digital challenge.

The 2027 edition centres on organisations working with young people in Brussels. The event date is confirmed; venues and application details are still being prepared.

faq.question: Do Makers get paid for the day of work?
faq.body: Kind of. In drinks, delicious snacks and good vibes.
faq.html: Kind of. In drinks, delicious snacks and good vibes.

faq.question: Do organisations need to pay to participate?
faq.body: Nope. The Makers gift their time and talent to help Brussels. No strings attached.
faq.html: Nope. The Makers gift their time and talent to help Brussels. No strings attached.

faq.question: Is there a Bruzz article with video that can give me a sense of the vibe of the event?
faq.body: Yes, there is. [You can find it here](https://www.bruzz.be/samenleving/creatieve-marathon-make-mark-maakt-brussel-opnieuw-een-beetje-beter-2023-03-19).
faq.html: Yes, there is. You can find it here.

faq.question: Would you like to organize Make a Mark in your city?
faq.body: Go for it! It's already happening in tens of cities around the globe. You can find guides and checklists on the [global website of Make a Mark](https://www.letsmakeamark.org/).
faq.html: Go for it! It's already happening in tens of cities around the globe. You can find guides and checklists on the global website of Make a Mark.
